"""C/C++ parser for ctags."""

import re

# C keywords that are not valid tag names
C_KEYWORDS = frozenset([
    'auto', 'break', 'case', 'char', 'const', 'continue', 'default', 'do',
    'double', 'else', 'enum', 'extern', 'float', 'for', 'goto', 'if',
    'inline', 'int', 'long', 'register', 'restrict', 'return', 'short',
    'signed', 'sizeof', 'static', 'struct', 'switch', 'typedef', 'union',
    'unsigned', 'void', 'volatile', 'while', '_Bool', '_Complex', '_Imaginary',
    '__attribute__', '__extension__', '__inline__', '__inline', '__volatile__',
    '__const', '__restrict', '__signed__', 'asm', '__asm__', '__asm',
])

CPP_KEYWORDS = C_KEYWORDS | frozenset([
    'bool', 'catch', 'class', 'constexpr', 'const_cast', 'delete',
    'dynamic_cast', 'explicit', 'export', 'false', 'friend', 'mutable',
    'namespace', 'new', 'noexcept', 'nullptr', 'operator', 'override',
    'private', 'protected', 'public', 'reinterpret_cast', 'static_assert',
    'static_cast', 'template', 'this', 'throw', 'true', 'try', 'typeid',
    'typename', 'using', 'virtual', 'wchar_t', 'final', 'alignas', 'alignof',
    'thread_local', 'decltype', 'concept', 'requires', 'consteval', 'constinit',
    'char8_t', 'char16_t', 'char32_t', 'co_await', 'co_return', 'co_yield',
])

# Type keywords that can appear in declarations
TYPE_QUALS = frozenset(['const', 'volatile', 'restrict', '__const', '__volatile__', '__restrict'])
TYPE_SPECS = frozenset(['unsigned', 'signed', 'long', 'short', 'int', 'char', 'float',
                        'double', 'void', 'bool', '_Bool', 'auto', 'wchar_t'])
STORAGE_SPECS = frozenset(['static', 'extern', 'register', 'auto', '__attribute__'])
FUNC_SPECS = frozenset(['inline', '__inline__', '__inline', 'explicit', 'virtual',
                        'constexpr', 'consteval', 'constinit', 'override', 'final'])


def remove_comments(text):
    """Remove C/C++ comments from text, preserving line count."""
    result = []
    i = 0
    n = len(text)
    
    while i < n:
        if text[i:i+2] == '/*':
            # Find end of block comment
            end = text.find('*/', i + 2)
            if end < 0:
                # Unterminated comment
                newlines = text[i:].count('\n')
                result.append('\n' * newlines)
                break
            # Count newlines in comment
            newlines = text[i:end+2].count('\n')
            result.append('\n' * newlines)
            i = end + 2
        elif text[i:i+2] == '//':
            # Line comment - find end of line
            end = text.find('\n', i)
            if end < 0:
                break
            result.append('\n')
            i = end + 1
        elif text[i] == '"':
            # String literal
            result.append('"')
            i += 1
            while i < n:
                if text[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < n:
                    result.append(text[i])
                    result.append(text[i+1])
                    i += 2
                elif text[i] == '"':
                    result.append('"')
                    i += 1
                    break
                else:
                    if text[i] == '\n':
                        result.append('\n')
                    else:
                        result.append('X')  # Replace char content to avoid false matches
                    i += 1
        elif text[i] == "'":
            # Char literal
            result.append("'")
            i += 1
            while i < n:
                if text[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < n:
                    result.append(text[i])
                    result.append(text[i+1])
                    i += 2
                elif text[i] == "'":
                    result.append("'")
                    i += 1
                    break
                else:
                    if text[i] == '\n':
                        result.append('\n')
                    else:
                        result.append('X')
                    i += 1
        else:
            result.append(text[i])
            i += 1
    
    return ''.join(result)


def make_macro_pattern(line, macro_name):
    """Create the ctags pattern for a #define line."""
    # Pattern rules for macros:
    # #define NAME        → /^#define NAME$/  (no space/value after)
    # #define NAME value  → /^#define NAME /  (space before value, stop at value)
    # #define NAME(...)   → /^#define NAME(/  (stop at paren)
    
    stripped = line.rstrip()
    # Find the macro name in the line
    idx = line.find('#')
    if idx < 0:
        return stripped
    
    define_match = re.match(r'#\s*define\s+' + re.escape(macro_name), line)
    if not define_match:
        return stripped[:96] if len(stripped) > 96 else stripped
    
    after_name = line[define_match.end():]
    
    if not after_name or after_name[0] in ('\n', '\r', ''):
        # No value or args: use full line
        return stripped
    elif after_name[0] == '(':
        # Function-like macro: end at opening paren
        return ('#define ' + macro_name + '(').strip()
        # Actually use the original indentation:
        prefix = line[:define_match.start() + 1]  # up to '#'
        return (prefix + 'define ' + macro_name + '(').rstrip()
    elif after_name[0] == ' ' or after_name[0] == '\t':
        # Object-like macro with value: end at space/tab
        return line[:define_match.end()].rstrip() + ' '
    else:
        return stripped


def parse_c(filename, raw_lines, tags, lang, opts):
    """Parse C/C++ file."""
    from ctags import Tag
    
    is_cpp = lang in ('C++', 'CUDA')
    keywords = CPP_KEYWORDS if is_cpp else C_KEYWORDS
    lim = opts.pattern_length_limit
    
    def make_pat(s):
        s = s.rstrip('\r\n')
        return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    def add(name, lineno, pattern, kind, kind_name, scope='', scope_kind='',
            scope_kind_name='', typeref='', file_scope=False):
        if not name or name in keywords:
            return
        if not re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_~]', name):
            return
        tags.append(Tag(
            name=name, file=filename, line=lineno,
            pattern=make_pat(pattern), kind=kind, kind_name=kind_name,
            scope=scope, scope_kind=scope_kind, scope_kind_name=scope_kind_name,
            typeref=typeref, file_scope=file_scope, lang=lang
        ))
    
    lines = raw_lines
    n = len(lines)
    
    # State machine
    brace_depth = 0  # current brace depth
    
    # Scope stack: entries are dicts
    # Each entry: {name, kind_char, kind_name, depth, file_scope, qual_name}
    # 'depth' is the brace_depth BEFORE the opening brace
    struct_stack = []  # stack of active struct/union/enum/class scopes
    
    def get_struct_scope():
        """Get current struct/class scope info."""
        if not struct_stack:
            return '', '', '', False
        top = struct_stack[-1]
        return top['qual_name'], top['kind_char'], top['kind_name'], top['file_scope']
    
    # Typedef tracking: when we see "typedef struct/union/enum {"
    # we need to remember so that "} Name;" creates typedef
    # Stack: (anon_name, kind_char, kind_name, depth_of_opening_brace)
    typedef_pending = []
    
    # Anonymous name counter
    anon_counter = [0]
    
    def gen_anon(kind_char):
        """Generate anonymous type name."""
        anon_counter[0] += 1
        kinds_sorted = sorted('defghlmpstuvxz')
        try:
            kind_idx = kinds_sorted.index(kind_char.lower())
        except ValueError:
            kind_idx = 0
        h = 5381
        for c in filename:
            h = ((h << 5) + h) ^ ord(c)
            h &= 0xFFFFFFFF
        suffix = anon_counter[0] * 256 + kind_idx
        return '__anon%08x%04x' % (h, suffix)
    
    # Namespace/class stack for C++
    scope_stack = []  # list of {name, kind_char, kind_name, qual_name, depth, file_scope}
    
    def get_cpp_scope():
        """Get current C++ scope (namespace/class)."""
        if not scope_stack:
            return '', '', ''
        top = scope_stack[-1]
        return top['qual_name'], top['kind_char'], top['kind_name']
    
    # Multi-line preprocessor handling
    in_macro_continuation = False
    
    # Process lines
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        line_raw = lines[i]
        lineno = i + 1
        
        # Count braces in this line
        in_str = False
        in_chr = False
        line_stripped = line_raw  # use raw for pattern generation
        
        # Count braces (simplified - doesn't handle all edge cases)
        new_opens = 0
        new_closes = 0
        for ch in line_raw:
            if in_str:
                if ch == '\\':
                    pass  # simplified
                elif ch == '"':
                    in_str = False
            elif in_chr:
                if ch == "'":
                    in_chr = False
            elif ch == '"':
                in_str = True
            elif ch == "'":
                in_chr = True
            elif ch == '{':
                new_opens += 1
            elif ch == '}':
                new_closes += 1
        
        prev_depth = brace_depth
        brace_depth += new_opens - new_closes
        if brace_depth < 0:
            brace_depth = 0
        
        # Pop struct stack entries that are no longer valid
        while struct_stack and struct_stack[-1]['depth'] >= brace_depth:
            struct_stack.pop()
        
        # Pop C++ scope stack entries
        while scope_stack and scope_stack[-1]['depth'] >= brace_depth:
            scope_stack.pop()
        
        # Check typedef pending - when brace depth decreases to pending depth level
        # and we see "} Name;"
        if typedef_pending and new_closes > 0:
            # Check each pending typedef
            for tp_idx in range(len(typedef_pending) - 1, -1, -1):
                tp = typedef_pending[tp_idx]
                if brace_depth <= tp[3] - 1:
                    # This typedef's closing brace was just passed
                    # Try to match } Name;
                    m = re.search(r'\}\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*;', line_raw)
                    if m:
                        typedef_nm = m.group(1)
                        anon_nm = tp[0]
                        kind_ch = tp[1]
                        kind_nm = tp[2]
                        typeref = kind_nm + ':' + anon_nm
                        
                        # Get parent scope
                        s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                        if not s_nm:
                            s_nm, s_kc, s_kn, _ = get_struct_scope()
                        
                        add(typedef_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 't', 'typedef',
                            scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                            typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)
                        typedef_pending.pop(tp_idx)
                    break
        
        # Process the line (use stripped version for matching)
        line = re.sub(r'//.*$', '', line_raw)
        # Remove block comments (simplified)
        line = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', ' ', line)
        stripped = line.strip()
        
        if not stripped:
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # --- Preprocessor ---
        if stripped.startswith('#'):
            # #define
            m = re.match(r'#\s*define\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)', stripped)
            if m:
                mac_name = m.group(1)
                # Build macro pattern
                pat = _macro_pattern(line_raw, mac_name, lim)
                s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                add(mac_name, lineno, pat, 'd', 'macro',
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn, file_scope=True)
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # Only process at depth 0 (top level) or inside struct/class/enum/union
        # Functions at depth 0 have body at depth 1, which we skip for nested items
        
        # --- Namespace (C++) ---
        if is_cpp and brace_depth == prev_depth and '{' in line:
            m = re.match(r'\bnamespace\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:::[A-Za-z_]\w*)*)\s*(?:\{|$)', stripped)
            if m:
                ns_name = m.group(1)
                s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                add(ns_name, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'n', 'namespace',
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn, file_scope=True)
                depth_before = brace_depth - new_opens
                qual = (s_nm + '::' + ns_name) if s_nm else ns_name
                scope_stack.append({
                    'name': ns_name, 'kind_char': 'n', 'kind_name': 'namespace',
                    'qual_name': qual, 'depth': depth_before, 'file_scope': True
                })
                i += 1
                continue
        
        # --- C++ class ---
        if is_cpp and prev_depth <= 1:
            m = re.match(r'\b(?:class|struct)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*(?:final\s*)?(?::[^{]*)?\s*\{', stripped)
            if m and not re.match(r'\btypedef\b', stripped):
                class_nm = m.group(1)
                if class_nm not in keywords:
                    s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                    if not s_nm:

                        s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2

                    kn = 'class' if kc == 'c' else 'struct'
                    fs = bool(s_nm)
                    
                    add(class_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), kc, kn,
                        scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                        file_scope=fs)
                    
                    depth_before = brace_depth - new_opens
                    qual = (s_nm + '::' + class_nm) if s_nm else class_nm
                    scope_stack.append({
                        'name': class_nm, 'kind_char': kc, 'kind_name': kn,
                        'qual_name': qual, 'depth': depth_before, 'file_scope': fs
                    })
                    struct_stack.append({
                        'name': class_nm, 'kind_char': kc, 'kind_name': kn,
                        'qual_name': qual, 'depth': depth_before, 'file_scope': fs
                    })
                    i += 1
                    continue
        
        # --- Typedef ---
        if re.match(r'\btypedef\b', stripped):
            # typedef enum/struct/union { ... } Name;  (multi-line)
            m = re.match(r'\btypedef\s+(struct|union|enum)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)?\s*\{', stripped)
            if m:
                kind_word = m.group(1)
                struct_name = m.group(2)
                kc = {'struct': 's', 'union': 'u', 'enum': 'g'}[kind_word]
                kn = kind_word
                
                s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()

                    s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2
                
                if struct_name:

                else:

                add(anon_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), kc, kn,

                qual = (s_nm + '::' + anon_nm) if s_nm else anon_nm
                struct_stack.append({

    stripped = line_raw.rstrip('\r\n')

        if not after.strip():
            # No value: use full line

        elif after[0] == '(':
            # Function-like macro
            result = stripped[:m.end()] + '('
        elif after[0] in (' ', '\t'):
            # Object-like macro with value
            result = stripped[:m.end()] + ' '
        else:
            result = stripped
    
    if lim > 0 and len(result) > lim:
        result = result[:lim]
    return result

    """Build a typeref string from a type expression."""
    type_str = type_str.strip()
    
    # Function pointer: TYPE (*)(PARAMS)
    fp_m = re.match(r'(.*?)\s*\(\s*\*\s*\)\s*\(([^)]*)\)', type_str)
    if fp_m:
        ret = fp_m.group(1).strip()
        params = fp_m.group(2).strip()

            re.sub(r'\s+\w+$', '', p.strip()) if re.search(r'\w+\s+\w+', p) else p.strip()
            for p in params.split(',')
        ) if params else ''
        return 'typename:' + ret + ' (*)(' + params_normalized + ')'
    
    # Struct/union/enum reference
    if type_str.startswith('struct '):
        return 'struct:' + type_str[7:].strip()
    elif type_str.startswith('union '):
        return 'union:' + type_str[6:].strip()
    elif type_str.startswith('enum '):
        return 'enum:' + type_str[5:].strip()
    else:

```
def _macro_pattern(line_raw, macro_name, lim):
    """Build the pattern for a #define line."""
    stripped = line_raw.rstrip('\r\n')
    
    # Find position after macro name
    m = re.search(r'#\s*define\s+' + re.escape(macro_name), stripped)
    if not m:
        result = stripped
    else:
        after = stripped[m.end():]
        if not after.strip():
            # No value: use full line
            result = stripped
        elif after[0] == '(':
            # Function-like macro
            result = stripped[:m.end()] + '('
        elif after[0] in (' ', '\t'):
            # Object-like macro with value
            result = stripped[:m.end()] + ' '
        else:
            result = stripped
    
    if lim > 0 and len(result) > lim:
        result = result[:lim]
    return result


def _build_typeref(type_str):
    """Build a typeref string from a type expression."""
    type_str = type_str.strip()
    
    # Function pointer: TYPE (*)(PARAMS)
    fp_m = re.match(r'(.*?)\s*\(\s*\*\s*\)\s*\(([^)]*)\)', type_str)
    if fp_m:
        ret = fp_m.group(1).strip()
        params = fp_m.group(2).strip()
        # Normalize params: remove names, keep types
        params_normalized = ','.join(
            re.sub(r'\s+\w+$', '', p.strip()) if re.search(r'\w+\s+\w+', p) else p.strip()
            for p in params.split(',')
        ) if params else ''
        return 'typename:' + ret + ' (*)(' + params_normalized + ')'
    
    # Struct/union/enum reference
    if type_str.startswith('struct '):
        return 'struct:' + type_str[7:].strip()
    elif type_str.startswith('union '):
        return 'union:' + type_str[6:].strip()
    elif type_str.startswith('enum '):
        return 'enum:' + type_str[5:].strip()
    else:
        return 'typename:' + type_str


def _parse_members(body_str, lineno, line_raw, scope_nm, scope_kc, scope_kn, add, lim):
    """Parse members from an inline struct body."""
    def make_pat(s): s = s.rstrip('\r\n'); return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    # Simple member parsing
    for m in re.finditer(r'([\w\s*]+?)\s+(\w+)\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*;', body_str):
        type_part = m.group(1).strip()
        member_nm = m.group(2).strip()
        arr_dim = m.group(3)
        
        if member_nm and not member_nm in ('if', 'while', 'for', 'return'):
            if arr_dim is not None:
                typeref = 'typename:' + type_part + '[' + (arr_dim or '') + ']'
            else:
                typeref = 'typename:' + type_part
            
            add(member_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                scope=scope_nm, scope_kind=scope_kc, scope_kind_name=scope_kn,
                typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)


def _parse_member_decl(stripped, lineno, line_raw, scope_nm, scope_kc, scope_kn, add, keywords, lim):
    """Parse a struct/union member declaration."""
    def make_pat(s): s = s.rstrip('\r\n'); return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    # Skip nested struct/union/enum declarations (handled separately)
    if re.match(r'\b(?:struct|union|enum)\b', stripped):
        return

    # TYPE can be: unsigned int, struct Foo *, etc.
    m = re.match(
        r'((?:(?:const|volatile|unsigned|signed|long|short|struct\s+\w+|union\s+\w+|enum\s+\w+|\w+)\s+)*'
        r'[*&]*)\s*(\w+)\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*(?:;|,|=)',
        stripped
    )
    if m:
        type_part = m.group(1).strip().rstrip('*&').strip()
        member_nm = m.group(2).strip()
        arr_dim = m.group(3)
        
        if member_nm and member_nm not in keywords and not member_nm.startswith('_') * 0:
            # Build type pointer info
            ptr_part = ''
            tp_full = m.group(1).strip()
            if '*' in tp_full:
                ptr_part = ' *'
            
            # Check for struct/union pointer
            if type_part.startswith('struct '):
                struct_name = type_part[7:].strip()
                if ptr_part:
                    typeref = 'struct:' + struct_name + ptr_part
                else:
                    typeref = 'struct:' + struct_name
            elif type_part.startswith('union '):
                typeref = 'union:' + type_part[6:].strip()
            else:
                if arr_dim is not None:
                    typeref = 'typename:' + (type_part + ptr_part).strip() + '[' + (arr_dim or '') + ']'
                else:
                    typeref = 'typename:' + (type_part + ptr_part).strip()
            
            add(member_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                scope=scope_nm, scope_kind=scope_kc, scope_kind_name=scope_kn,
                typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)


def _parse_top_level(stripped, lineno, line_raw, is_cpp, keywords, add,

                     brace_depth, prev_depth, new_opens, lim):
    """Parse a top-level or namespace-level declaration."""
    def make_pat(s): s = s.rstrip('\r\n'); return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s

    if re.match(r'\b(?:if|else|for|while|do|switch|case|default|return|break|continue|goto)\b', stripped):

        r'(?:\s*[*&]+)?\s+)*(?:~?[*&]*)\s*)?'
        r'(~?[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:::[~A-Za-z_]\w*)*)\s*'
        r'\(([^)]*)\)\s*(?:const\s*)?(?:noexcept[^{]*)?(?:override\s*)?(?:final\s*)?\s*\{'

        ret_type = (m.group(2) or '').strip()

            return
        
        is_static = 'static' in quals_str
        
        if '::' in func_name_full:
            # Qualified method definition (outside class body)
            parts = func_name_full.rsplit('::', 1)
            scope_part = parts[0]
            func_nm = parts[1]
            
            # Determine scope kind (assume class unless we know it's namespace)
            sk = 'c'
            skn = 'class'

            s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()

                top = struct_stack[-1]
                add(func_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'f', 'function',
                    scope=top['qual_name'], scope_kind=top['kind_char'], scope_kind_name=top['kind_name'],
                    typeref='typename:' + (ret_type or 'void'), file_scope=top['file_scope'])
            else:
                add(func_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'f', 'function',
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                    typeref='typename:' + (ret_type or 'void'), file_scope=is_static)

    # Variable declaration: TYPE NAME [= VALUE];

    fp_var = re.match(
        r'^((?:(?:static|extern|const|volatile)\s+)*)'
        r'([\w\s*]+?)\s*\(\s*\*\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\)\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*(?:=.*)?;',
        stripped
    )
    if fp_var:
        quals_str = fp_var.group(1).strip()
        ret_type = fp_var.group(2).strip()
        var_nm = fp_var.group(3).strip()
        params = fp_var.group(4).strip()
        
        if var_nm not in keywords:
            # Normalize params
            params_norm = ','.join(p.strip() for p in params.split(',')) if params else ''
            typeref = 'typename:' + ret_type + ' (*)(' + params_norm + ')'
            
            is_static = 'static' in quals_str
            s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
            
            if struct_stack and struct_stack[-1]['kind_char'] in ('s', 'u', 'c'):
                top = struct_stack[-1]
                add(var_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                    scope=top['qual_name'], scope_kind=top['kind_char'], scope_kind_name=top['kind_name'],
                    typeref=typeref, file_scope=top['file_scope'])
            else:
                add(var_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'v', 'variable',
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                    typeref=typeref, file_scope=is_static)
        return
    
    # Regular variable declaration
    var_m = re.match(
        r'^((?:(?:static|extern|const|volatile|register|inline)\s+)*)'
        r'((?:(?:const|volatile|unsigned|signed|long|short|struct\s+\w+|union\s+\w+|enum\s+\w+|\w+)'
        r'(?:\s*[*&]+\s*)?)\s*[*&]*)\s+'
        r'([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*(?:=.*)?;',
        stripped
    )

        quals_str = var_m.group(1).strip()
        type_part = var_m.group(2).strip()
        var_nm = var_m.group(3).strip()
        arr_dim = var_m.group(4)

            is_static = 'static' in quals_str
            is_extern = 'extern' in quals_str
            
            # Build typeref

                typeref = 'typename:' + type_part + '[' + (arr_dim or '') + ']'
            elif type_part.startswith('struct '):
                typeref = 'struct:' + type_part[7:].strip()
            elif type_part.startswith('union '):
                typeref = 'union:' + type_part[6:].strip()
            else:

                    typeref = 'typename:' + base + ' ' + ptr
                else:

            s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
            
            if struct_stack and struct_stack[-1]['kind_char'] in ('s', 'u', 'c'):
                top = struct_stack[-1]
                add(var_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                    scope=top['qual_name'], scope_kind=top['kind_char'], scope_kind_name=top['kind_name'],
                    typeref=typeref, file_scope=top['file_scope'])
            else:

                        scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                        typeref=typeref, file_scope=is_static)
```

    '__attribute__', '__extension__', '__inline__', '__inline', '__volatile__',
    '__const', '__restrict', '__signed__', 'asm', '__asm__', '__asm',
])

CPP_KEYWORDS = C_KEYWORDS | frozenset([
    'bool', 'catch', 'class', 'constexpr', 'const_cast', 'delete',
    'dynamic_cast', 'explicit', 'export', 'false', 'friend', 'mutable',
    'namespace', 'new', 'noexcept', 'nullptr', 'operator', 'override',
    'private', 'protected', 'public', 'reinterpret_cast', 'static_assert',
    'static_cast', 'template', 'this', 'throw', 'true', 'try', 'typeid',
    'typename', 'using', 'virtual', 'wchar_t', 'final', 'alignas', 'alignof',
    'thread_local', 'decltype', 'concept', 'requires', 'consteval', 'constinit',
    'char8_t', 'char16_t', 'char32_t', 'co_await', 'co_return', 'co_yield',
])

# Type keywords that can appear in declarations
TYPE_QUALS = frozenset(['const', 'volatile', 'restrict', '__const', '__volatile__', '__restrict'])
TYPE_SPECS = frozenset(['unsigned', 'signed', 'long', 'short', 'int', 'char', 'float',
                        'double', 'void', 'bool', '_Bool', 'auto', 'wchar_t'])
STORAGE_SPECS = frozenset(['static', 'extern', 'register', 'auto', '__attribute__'])
FUNC_SPECS = frozenset(['inline', '__inline__', '__inline', 'explicit', 'virtual',
                        'constexpr', 'consteval', 'constinit', 'override', 'final'])


def remove_comments(text):
    """Remove C/C++ comments from text, preserving line count."""
    result = []
    i = 0
    n = len(text)
    
    while i < n:
        if text[i:i+2] == '/*':
            # Find end of block comment
            end = text.find('*/', i + 2)
            if end < 0:
                # Unterminated comment
                newlines = text[i:].count('\n')
                result.append('\n' * newlines)
                break
            # Count newlines in comment
            newlines = text[i:end+2].count('\n')
            result.append('\n' * newlines)
            i = end + 2
        elif text[i:i+2] == '//':
            # Line comment - find end of line
            end = text.find('\n', i)
            if end < 0:
                break
            result.append('\n')
            i = end + 1
        elif text[i] == '"':
            # String literal
            result.append('"')
            i += 1
            while i < n:
                if text[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < n:
                    result.append(text[i])
                    result.append(text[i+1])
                    i += 2
                elif text[i] == '"':
                    result.append('"')
                    i += 1
                    break
                else:
                    if text[i] == '\n':
                        result.append('\n')
                    else:
                        result.append('X')  # Replace char content to avoid false matches
                    i += 1
        elif text[i] == "'":
            # Char literal
            result.append("'")
            i += 1
            while i < n:
                if text[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < n:
                    result.append(text[i])
                    result.append(text[i+1])
                    i += 2
                elif text[i] == "'":
                    result.append("'")
                    i += 1
                    break
                else:
                    if text[i] == '\n':
                        result.append('\n')
                    else:
                        result.append('X')
                    i += 1
        else:
            result.append(text[i])
            i += 1
    
    return ''.join(result)


def make_macro_pattern(line, macro_name):
    """Create the ctags pattern for a #define line."""
    # Pattern rules for macros:
    # #define NAME        → /^#define NAME$/  (no space/value after)
    # #define NAME value  → /^#define NAME /  (space before value, stop at value)
    # #define NAME(...)   → /^#define NAME(/  (stop at paren)
    
    stripped = line.rstrip()
    # Find the macro name in the line
    idx = line.find('#')
    if idx < 0:
        return stripped
    
    define_match = re.match(r'#\s*define\s+' + re.escape(macro_name), line)
    if not define_match:
        return stripped[:96] if len(stripped) > 96 else stripped
    
    after_name = line[define_match.end():]
    
    if not after_name or after_name[0] in ('\n', '\r', ''):
        # No value or args: use full line
        return stripped
    elif after_name[0] == '(':
        # Function-like macro: end at opening paren
        return ('#define ' + macro_name + '(').strip()
        # Actually use the original indentation:
        prefix = line[:define_match.start() + 1]  # up to '#'
        return (prefix + 'define ' + macro_name + '(').rstrip()
    elif after_name[0] == ' ' or after_name[0] == '\t':
        # Object-like macro with value: end at space/tab
        return line[:define_match.end()].rstrip() + ' '
    else:
        return stripped


def parse_c(filename, raw_lines, tags, lang, opts):
    """Parse C/C++ file."""
    from ctags import Tag
    
    is_cpp = lang in ('C++', 'CUDA')
    keywords = CPP_KEYWORDS if is_cpp else C_KEYWORDS
    lim = opts.pattern_length_limit
    
    def make_pat(s):
        s = s.rstrip('\r\n')
        return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    def add(name, lineno, pattern, kind, kind_name, scope='', scope_kind='',
            scope_kind_name='', typeref='', file_scope=False):
        if not name or name in keywords:
            return
        if not re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_~]', name):
            return
        tags.append(Tag(
            name=name, file=filename, line=lineno,
            pattern=make_pat(pattern), kind=kind, kind_name=kind_name,
            scope=scope, scope_kind=scope_kind, scope_kind_name=scope_kind_name,
            typeref=typeref, file_scope=file_scope, lang=lang
        ))
    
    lines = raw_lines
    n = len(lines)
    
    # State machine
    brace_depth = 0  # current brace depth
    
    # Scope stack: entries are dicts
    # Each entry: {name, kind_char, kind_name, depth, file_scope, qual_name}
    # 'depth' is the brace_depth BEFORE the opening brace
    struct_stack = []  # stack of active struct/union/enum/class scopes
    
    def get_struct_scope():
        """Get current struct/class scope info."""
        if not struct_stack:
            return '', '', '', False
        top = struct_stack[-1]
        return top['qual_name'], top['kind_char'], top['kind_name'], top['file_scope']
    
    # Typedef tracking: when we see "typedef struct/union/enum {"
    # we need to remember so that "} Name;" creates typedef
    # Stack: (anon_name, kind_char, kind_name, depth_of_opening_brace)
    typedef_pending = []
    
    # Anonymous name counter
    anon_counter = [0]
    
    def gen_anon(kind_char):
        """Generate anonymous type name."""
        anon_counter[0] += 1
        kinds_sorted = sorted('defghlmpstuvxz')
        try:
            kind_idx = kinds_sorted.index(kind_char.lower())
        except ValueError:
            kind_idx = 0
        h = 5381
        for c in filename:
            h = ((h << 5) + h) ^ ord(c)
            h &= 0xFFFFFFFF
        suffix = anon_counter[0] * 256 + kind_idx
        return '__anon%08x%04x' % (h, suffix)
    
    # Namespace/class stack for C++
    scope_stack = []  # list of {name, kind_char, kind_name, qual_name, depth, file_scope}
    
    def get_cpp_scope():
        """Get current C++ scope (namespace/class)."""
        if not scope_stack:
            return '', '', ''
        top = scope_stack[-1]
        return top['qual_name'], top['kind_char'], top['kind_name']
    
    # Multi-line preprocessor handling
    in_macro_continuation = False
    
    # Process lines
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        line_raw = lines[i]
        lineno = i + 1
        
        # Count braces in this line
        in_str = False
        in_chr = False
        line_stripped = line_raw  # use raw for pattern generation
        
        # Count braces (simplified - doesn't handle all edge cases)
        new_opens = 0
        new_closes = 0
        for ch in line_raw:
            if in_str:
                if ch == '\\':
                    pass  # simplified
                elif ch == '"':
                    in_str = False
            elif in_chr:
                if ch == "'":
                    in_chr = False
            elif ch == '"':
                in_str = True
            elif ch == "'":
                in_chr = True
            elif ch == '{':
                new_opens += 1
            elif ch == '}':
                new_closes += 1
        
        prev_depth = brace_depth
        brace_depth += new_opens - new_closes
        if brace_depth < 0:
            brace_depth = 0
        
        # Pop struct stack entries that are no longer valid
        while struct_stack and struct_stack[-1]['depth'] >= brace_depth:
            struct_stack.pop()
        
        # Pop C++ scope stack entries
        while scope_stack and scope_stack[-1]['depth'] >= brace_depth:
            scope_stack.pop()
        
        # Check typedef pending - when brace depth decreases to pending depth level
        # and we see "} Name;"
        if typedef_pending and new_closes > 0:
            # Check each pending typedef
            for tp_idx in range(len(typedef_pending) - 1, -1, -1):
                tp = typedef_pending[tp_idx]
                if brace_depth <= tp[3] - 1:
                    # This typedef's closing brace was just passed
                    # Try to match } Name;
                    m = re.search(r'\}\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*;', line_raw)
                    if m:
                        typedef_nm = m.group(1)
                        anon_nm = tp[0]
                        kind_ch = tp[1]
                        kind_nm = tp[2]
                        typeref = kind_nm + ':' + anon_nm
                        
                        # Get parent scope
                        s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                        if not s_nm:
                            s_nm, s_kc, s_kn, _ = get_struct_scope()
                        
                        add(typedef_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 't', 'typedef',
                            scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                            typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)
                        typedef_pending.pop(tp_idx)
                    break
        
        # Process the line (use stripped version for matching)
        line = re.sub(r'//.*$', '', line_raw)
        # Remove block comments (simplified)
        line = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', ' ', line)
        stripped = line.strip()
        
        if not stripped:
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # --- Preprocessor ---
        if stripped.startswith('#'):
            # #define
            m = re.match(r'#\s*define\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)', stripped)
            if m:
                mac_name = m.group(1)
                # Build macro pattern
                pat = _macro_pattern(line_raw, mac_name, lim)
                s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                add(mac_name, lineno, pat, 'd', 'macro',
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn, file_scope=True)
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # Only process at depth 0 (top level) or inside struct/class/enum/union
        # Functions at depth 0 have body at depth 1, which we skip for nested items
        
        # --- Namespace (C++) ---
        if is_cpp and brace_depth == prev_depth and '{' in line:
            m = re.match(r'\bnamespace\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:::[A-Za-z_]\w*)*)\s*(?:\{|$)', stripped)
            if m:
                ns_name = m.group(1)
                s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                add(ns_name, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'n', 'namespace',
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn, file_scope=True)
                depth_before = brace_depth - new_opens
                qual = (s_nm + '::' + ns_name) if s_nm else ns_name
                scope_stack.append({
                    'name': ns_name, 'kind_char': 'n', 'kind_name': 'namespace',
                    'qual_name': qual, 'depth': depth_before, 'file_scope': True
                })
                i += 1
                continue
        
        # --- C++ class ---
        if is_cpp and prev_depth <= 1:
            m = re.match(r'\b(?:class|struct)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*(?:final\s*)?(?::[^{]*)?\s*\{', stripped)
            if m and not re.match(r'\btypedef\b', stripped):
                class_nm = m.group(1)
                if class_nm not in keywords:
                    s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                    if not s_nm:
                        s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2, fs2 = get_struct_scope()
                        s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2
                    
                    kc = 'c' if stripped.startswith('class') else 's'
                    kn = 'class' if kc == 'c' else 'struct'
                    fs = bool(s_nm)
                    
                    add(class_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), kc, kn,
                        scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                        file_scope=fs)
                    
                    depth_before = brace_depth - new_opens
                    qual = (s_nm + '::' + class_nm) if s_nm else class_nm
                    scope_stack.append({
                        'name': class_nm, 'kind_char': kc, 'kind_name': kn,
                        'qual_name': qual, 'depth': depth_before, 'file_scope': fs
                    })
                    struct_stack.append({
                        'name': class_nm, 'kind_char': kc, 'kind_name': kn,
                        'qual_name': qual, 'depth': depth_before, 'file_scope': fs
                    })
                    i += 1
                    continue
        
        # --- Typedef ---
        if re.match(r'\btypedef\b', stripped):
            # typedef enum/struct/union { ... } Name;  (multi-line)
            m = re.match(r'\btypedef\s+(struct|union|enum)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)?\s*\{', stripped)
            if m:
                kind_word = m.group(1)
                struct_name = m.group(2)
                kc = {'struct': 's', 'union': 'u', 'enum': 'g'}[kind_word]
                kn = kind_word
                
                s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                if not s_nm:
                    s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2, _ = get_struct_scope()
                    s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2
                
                if struct_name:
                    anon_nm = struct_name
                else:
                    anon_nm = gen_anon(kc)
                
                add(anon_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), kc, kn,
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn, file_scope=True)
                
                depth_before = brace_depth - new_opens
                qual = (s_nm + '::' + anon_nm) if s_nm else anon_nm
                struct_stack.append({
                    'name': anon_nm, 'kind_char': kc, 'kind_name': kn,
                    'qual_name': qual, 'depth': depth_before, 'file_scope': True
                })
                typedef_pending.append((anon_nm, kc, kn, brace_depth))
                i += 1
                continue
            
            # Check for same-line: typedef struct { ... } Name;
            m_inline = re.match(r'\btypedef\s+(struct|union|enum)\s*\{([^}]*)\}\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*;', stripped)
            if m_inline:
                kind_word = m_inline.group(1)
                body = m_inline.group(2)
                typedef_nm = m_inline.group(3)
                kc = {'struct': 's', 'union': 'u', 'enum': 'g'}[kind_word]
                kn = kind_word
                anon_nm = gen_anon(kc)
                
                s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                
                add(anon_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), kc, kn,
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn, file_scope=True)
                add(typedef_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 't', 'typedef',
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                    typeref=kn + ':' + anon_nm, file_scope=True)
                
                # Process inline members
                _parse_members(body, lineno, line_raw, anon_nm, kc, kn, add, lim)
                i += 1
                continue
            
            # typedef TYPE NAME; (simple)
            m_simple = re.match(r'\btypedef\b\s+(.+?)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*;', stripped)
            if m_simple:
                type_str = m_simple.group(1).strip()
                typedef_nm = m_simple.group(2).strip()
                
                if typedef_nm not in keywords:
                    typeref = _build_typeref(type_str)
                    s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                    if not s_nm:
                        s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2, _ = get_struct_scope()
                        s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2
                    
                    add(typedef_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 't', 'typedef',
                        scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                        typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # --- Struct/Union declaration ---
        m = re.match(r'\b(struct|union|enum)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*(\{)', stripped)
        if m and not re.match(r'\btypedef\b', stripped):
            kind_word = m.group(1)
            type_name = m.group(2)
            kc = {'struct': 's', 'union': 'u', 'enum': 'g'}[kind_word]
            kn = kind_word
            
            if type_name not in keywords:
                s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                if not s_nm:
                    s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2, _ = get_struct_scope()
                    s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2
                
                add(type_name, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), kc, kn,
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn, file_scope=True)
                
                depth_before = brace_depth - new_opens
                qual = (s_nm + '::' + type_name) if s_nm else type_name
                struct_stack.append({
                    'name': type_name, 'kind_char': kc, 'kind_name': kn,
                    'qual_name': qual, 'depth': depth_before, 'file_scope': True
                })
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # --- Struct/Union members (inside struct scope) ---
        if struct_stack:
            top = struct_stack[-1]
            if top['depth'] < brace_depth <= top['depth'] + 1:
                scope_nm = top['qual_name']
                scope_kc = top['kind_char']
                scope_kn = top['kind_name']
                
                if scope_kc == 'g':
                    # Enum values
                    for em in re.finditer(r'\b([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*(?:=\s*[^,}]+)?(?:,|$)', stripped.rstrip(',')):
                        val_name = em.group(1)
                        if val_name not in keywords and val_name not in ('__attribute__',):
                            add(val_name, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'e', 'enumerator',
                                scope=scope_nm, scope_kind=scope_kc, scope_kind_name=scope_kn,
                                file_scope=True)
                elif scope_kc in ('s', 'u'):
                    # Struct/union members
                    _parse_member_decl(stripped, lineno, line_raw, scope_nm, scope_kc, scope_kn,
                                       add, keywords, lim)
                elif scope_kc in ('c',):
                    # C++ class members (methods, fields)
                    pass  # handled by function/variable parsing below
                i += 1
                continue
        
        # --- Enum values at depth 1 (inside enum body) ---
        
        # --- Functions and variables at top level ---
        if prev_depth == 0 or (is_cpp and prev_depth <= len(scope_stack)):
            _parse_top_level(stripped, lineno, line_raw, is_cpp, keywords,
                             add, struct_stack, scope_stack, get_cpp_scope,
                             get_struct_scope, brace_depth, prev_depth, new_opens, lim)
        
        i += 1


def _macro_pattern(line_raw, macro_name, lim):
    """Build the pattern for a #define line."""
    stripped = line_raw.rstrip('\r\n')
    
    # Find position after macro name
    m = re.search(r'#\s*define\s+' + re.escape(macro_name), stripped)
    if not m:
        result = stripped
    else:
        after = stripped[m.end():]
        if not after.strip():
            # No value: use full line
            result = stripped
        elif after[0] == '(':
            # Function-like macro
            result = stripped[:m.end()] + '('
        elif after[0] in (' ', '\t'):
            # Object-like macro with value
            result = stripped[:m.end()] + ' '
        else:
            result = stripped
    
    if lim > 0 and len(result) > lim:
        result = result[:lim]
    return result


def _build_typeref(type_str):
    """Build a typeref string from a type expression."""
    type_str = type_str.strip()
    
    # Function pointer: TYPE (*)(PARAMS)
    fp_m = re.match(r'(.*?)\s*\(\s*\*\s*\)\s*\(([^)]*)\)', type_str)
    if fp_m:
        ret = fp_m.group(1).strip()
        params = fp_m.group(2).strip()
        # Normalize params: remove names, keep types
        params_normalized = ','.join(
            re.sub(r'\s+\w+$', '', p.strip()) if re.search(r'\w+\s+\w+', p) else p.strip()
            for p in params.split(',')
        ) if params else ''
        return 'typename:' + ret + ' (*)(' + params_normalized + ')'
    
    # Struct/union/enum reference
    if type_str.startswith('struct '):
        return 'struct:' + type_str[7:].strip()
    elif type_str.startswith('union '):
        return 'union:' + type_str[6:].strip()
    elif type_str.startswith('enum '):
        return 'enum:' + type_str[5:].strip()
    else:
        return 'typename:' + type_str


def _parse_members(body_str, lineno, line_raw, scope_nm, scope_kc, scope_kn, add, lim):
    """Parse members from an inline struct body."""
    def make_pat(s): s = s.rstrip('\r\n'); return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    # Simple member parsing
    for m in re.finditer(r'([\w\s*]+?)\s+(\w+)\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*;', body_str):
        type_part = m.group(1).strip()
        member_nm = m.group(2).strip()
        arr_dim = m.group(3)
        
        if member_nm and not member_nm in ('if', 'while', 'for', 'return'):
            if arr_dim is not None:
                typeref = 'typename:' + type_part + '[' + (arr_dim or '') + ']'
            else:
                typeref = 'typename:' + type_part
            
            add(member_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                scope=scope_nm, scope_kind=scope_kc, scope_kind_name=scope_kn,
                typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)


def _parse_member_decl(stripped, lineno, line_raw, scope_nm, scope_kc, scope_kn, add, keywords, lim):
    """Parse a struct/union member declaration."""
    def make_pat(s): s = s.rstrip('\r\n'); return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    # Skip nested struct/union/enum declarations (handled separately)
    if re.match(r'\b(?:struct|union|enum)\b', stripped):
        return
    
    # Match: TYPE *NAME[DIMS] ;
    # TYPE can be: unsigned int, struct Foo *, etc.
    m = re.match(
        r'((?:(?:const|volatile|unsigned|signed|long|short|struct\s+\w+|union\s+\w+|enum\s+\w+|\w+)\s+)*'
        r'[*&]*)\s*(\w+)\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*(?:;|,|=)',
        stripped
    )
    if m:
        type_part = m.group(1).strip().rstrip('*&').strip()
        member_nm = m.group(2).strip()
        arr_dim = m.group(3)
        
        if member_nm and member_nm not in keywords and not member_nm.startswith('_') * 0:
            # Build type pointer info
            ptr_part = ''
            tp_full = m.group(1).strip()
            if '*' in tp_full:
                ptr_part = ' *'
            
            # Check for struct/union pointer
            if type_part.startswith('struct '):
                struct_name = type_part[7:].strip()
                if ptr_part:
                    typeref = 'struct:' + struct_name + ptr_part
                else:
                    typeref = 'struct:' + struct_name
            elif type_part.startswith('union '):
                typeref = 'union:' + type_part[6:].strip()
            else:
                if arr_dim is not None:
                    typeref = 'typename:' + (type_part + ptr_part).strip() + '[' + (arr_dim or '') + ']'
                else:
                    typeref = 'typename:' + (type_part + ptr_part).strip()
            
            add(member_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                scope=scope_nm, scope_kind=scope_kc, scope_kind_name=scope_kn,
                typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)


def _parse_top_level(stripped, lineno, line_raw, is_cpp, keywords, add,

def remove_comments(text):
    """Remove C/C++ comments from text, preserving line count."""
    result = []
    i = 0
    n = len(text)
    
    while i < n:
        if text[i:i+2] == '/*':
            # Find end of block comment
            end = text.find('*/', i + 2)
            if end < 0:
                # Unterminated comment
                newlines = text[i:].count('\n')
                result.append('\n' * newlines)
                break
            # Count newlines in comment
            newlines = text[i:end+2].count('\n')
            result.append('\n' * newlines)
            i = end + 2
        elif text[i:i+2] == '//':
            # Line comment - find end of line
            end = text.find('\n', i)
            if end < 0:
                break
            result.append('\n')
            i = end + 1
        elif text[i] == '"':
            # String literal
            result.append('"')
            i += 1
            while i < n:
                if text[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < n:
                    result.append(text[i])
                    result.append(text[i+1])
                    i += 2
                elif text[i] == '"':
                    result.append('"')
                    i += 1
                    break
                else:
                    if text[i] == '\n':
                        result.append('\n')
                    else:
                        result.append('X')  # Replace char content to avoid false matches
                    i += 1
        elif text[i] == "'":
            # Char literal
            result.append("'")
            i += 1
            while i < n:
                if text[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < n:
                    result.append(text[i])
                    result.append(text[i+1])
                    i += 2
                elif text[i] == "'":
                    result.append("'")
                    i += 1
                    break
                else:
                    if text[i] == '\n':
                        result.append('\n')
                    else:
                        result.append('X')
                    i += 1
        else:
            result.append(text[i])
            i += 1
    
    return ''.join(result)


def make_macro_pattern(line, macro_name):
    """Create the ctags pattern for a #define line."""
    # Pattern rules for macros:
    # #define NAME        → /^#define NAME$/  (no space/value after)
    # #define NAME value  → /^#define NAME /  (space before value, stop at value)
    # #define NAME(...)   → /^#define NAME(/  (stop at paren)
    
    stripped = line.rstrip()
    # Find the macro name in the line
    idx = line.find('#')
    if idx < 0:
        return stripped
    
    define_match = re.match(r'#\s*define\s+' + re.escape(macro_name), line)
    if not define_match:
        return stripped[:96] if len(stripped) > 96 else stripped
    
    after_name = line[define_match.end():]
    
    if not after_name or after_name[0] in ('\n', '\r', ''):
        # No value or args: use full line
        return stripped
    elif after_name[0] == '(':
        # Function-like macro: end at opening paren
        return ('#define ' + macro_name + '(').strip()
        # Actually use the original indentation:
        prefix = line[:define_match.start() + 1]  # up to '#'
        return (prefix + 'define ' + macro_name + '(').rstrip()
    elif after_name[0] == ' ' or after_name[0] == '\t':
        # Object-like macro with value: end at space/tab
        return line[:define_match.end()].rstrip() + ' '
    else:
        return stripped

                    s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                    if not s_nm:
                        s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2, _ = get_struct_scope()
                        s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2
                    
                    add(typedef_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 't', 'typedef',
                        scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                        typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # --- Struct/Union declaration ---
        m = re.match(r'\b(struct|union|enum)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*(\{)', stripped)
        if m and not re.match(r'\btypedef\b', stripped):
            kind_word = m.group(1)
            type_name = m.group(2)
            kc = {'struct': 's', 'union': 'u', 'enum': 'g'}[kind_word]
            kn = kind_word
            
            if type_name not in keywords:
                s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
                if not s_nm:
                    s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2, _ = get_struct_scope()
                    s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = s_nm2, s_kc2, s_kn2
                
                add(type_name, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), kc, kn,
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn, file_scope=True)
                
                depth_before = brace_depth - new_opens
                qual = (s_nm + '::' + type_name) if s_nm else type_name
                struct_stack.append({
                    'name': type_name, 'kind_char': kc, 'kind_name': kn,
                    'qual_name': qual, 'depth': depth_before, 'file_scope': True
                })
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # --- Struct/Union members (inside struct scope) ---
        if struct_stack:
            top = struct_stack[-1]
            if top['depth'] < brace_depth <= top['depth'] + 1:
                scope_nm = top['qual_name']
                scope_kc = top['kind_char']
                scope_kn = top['kind_name']
                
                if scope_kc == 'g':
                    # Enum values
                    for em in re.finditer(r'\b([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*(?:=\s*[^,}]+)?(?:,|$)', stripped.rstrip(',')):
                        val_name = em.group(1)
                        if val_name not in keywords and val_name not in ('__attribute__',):
                            add(val_name, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'e', 'enumerator',
                                scope=scope_nm, scope_kind=scope_kc, scope_kind_name=scope_kn,
                                file_scope=True)
                elif scope_kc in ('s', 'u'):
                    # Struct/union members
                    _parse_member_decl(stripped, lineno, line_raw, scope_nm, scope_kc, scope_kn,
                                       add, keywords, lim)
                elif scope_kc in ('c',):
                    # C++ class members (methods, fields)
                    pass  # handled by function/variable parsing below
                i += 1
                continue
        
        # --- Enum values at depth 1 (inside enum body) ---
        
        # --- Functions and variables at top level ---
        if prev_depth == 0 or (is_cpp and prev_depth <= len(scope_stack)):
            _parse_top_level(stripped, lineno, line_raw, is_cpp, keywords,
                             add, struct_stack, scope_stack, get_cpp_scope,
                             get_struct_scope, brace_depth, prev_depth, new_opens, lim)
        
        i += 1


def _macro_pattern(line_raw, macro_name, lim):
    """Build the pattern for a #define line."""
    stripped = line_raw.rstrip('\r\n')
    
    # Find position after macro name
    m = re.search(r'#\s*define\s+' + re.escape(macro_name), stripped)
    if not m:
        result = stripped
    else:
        after = stripped[m.end():]
        if not after.strip():
            # No value: use full line
            result = stripped
        elif after[0] == '(':
            # Function-like macro
            result = stripped[:m.end()] + '('
        elif after[0] in (' ', '\t'):
            # Object-like macro with value
            result = stripped[:m.end()] + ' '
        else:
            result = stripped
    
    if lim > 0 and len(result) > lim:
        result = result[:lim]
    return result


def _build_typeref(type_str):
    """Build a typeref string from a type expression."""
    type_str = type_str.strip()
    
    # Function pointer: TYPE (*)(PARAMS)
    fp_m = re.match(r'(.*?)\s*\(\s*\*\s*\)\s*\(([^)]*)\)', type_str)
    if fp_m:
        ret = fp_m.group(1).strip()
        params = fp_m.group(2).strip()
        # Normalize params: remove names, keep types
        params_normalized = ','.join(
            re.sub(r'\s+\w+$', '', p.strip()) if re.search(r'\w+\s+\w+', p) else p.strip()
            for p in params.split(',')
        ) if params else ''
        return 'typename:' + ret + ' (*)(' + params_normalized + ')'
    
    # Struct/union/enum reference
    if type_str.startswith('struct '):
        return 'struct:' + type_str[7:].strip()
    elif type_str.startswith('union '):
        return 'union:' + type_str[6:].strip()
    elif type_str.startswith('enum '):
        return 'enum:' + type_str[5:].strip()
    else:
        return 'typename:' + type_str


def _parse_members(body_str, lineno, line_raw, scope_nm, scope_kc, scope_kn, add, lim):
    """Parse members from an inline struct body."""
    def make_pat(s): s = s.rstrip('\r\n'); return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    # Simple member parsing
    for m in re.finditer(r'([\w\s*]+?)\s+(\w+)\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*;', body_str):
        type_part = m.group(1).strip()
        member_nm = m.group(2).strip()
        arr_dim = m.group(3)
        
        if member_nm and not member_nm in ('if', 'while', 'for', 'return'):
            if arr_dim is not None:
                typeref = 'typename:' + type_part + '[' + (arr_dim or '') + ']'
            else:
                typeref = 'typename:' + type_part
            
            add(member_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                scope=scope_nm, scope_kind=scope_kc, scope_kind_name=scope_kn,
                typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)


def _parse_member_decl(stripped, lineno, line_raw, scope_nm, scope_kc, scope_kn, add, keywords, lim):
    """Parse a struct/union member declaration."""
    def make_pat(s): s = s.rstrip('\r\n'); return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    # Skip nested struct/union/enum declarations (handled separately)
    if re.match(r'\b(?:struct|union|enum)\b', stripped):
        return
    
    # Match: TYPE *NAME[DIMS] ;
    # TYPE can be: unsigned int, struct Foo *, etc.
    m = re.match(
        r'((?:(?:const|volatile|unsigned|signed|long|short|struct\s+\w+|union\s+\w+|enum\s+\w+|\w+)\s+)*'
        r'[*&]*)\s*(\w+)\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*(?:;|,|=)',
        stripped
    )
    if m:
        type_part = m.group(1).strip().rstrip('*&').strip()
        member_nm = m.group(2).strip()
        arr_dim = m.group(3)
        
        if member_nm and member_nm not in keywords and not member_nm.startswith('_') * 0:
            # Build type pointer info
            ptr_part = ''
            tp_full = m.group(1).strip()
            if '*' in tp_full:
                ptr_part = ' *'
            
            # Check for struct/union pointer
            if type_part.startswith('struct '):
                struct_name = type_part[7:].strip()
                if ptr_part:
                    typeref = 'struct:' + struct_name + ptr_part
                else:
                    typeref = 'struct:' + struct_name
            elif type_part.startswith('union '):
                typeref = 'union:' + type_part[6:].strip()
            else:
                if arr_dim is not None:
                    typeref = 'typename:' + (type_part + ptr_part).strip() + '[' + (arr_dim or '') + ']'
                else:
                    typeref = 'typename:' + (type_part + ptr_part).strip()
            
            add(member_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                scope=scope_nm, scope_kind=scope_kc, scope_kind_name=scope_kn,
                typeref=typeref, file_scope=True)


def _parse_top_level(stripped, lineno, line_raw, is_cpp, keywords, add,
                     struct_stack, scope_stack, get_cpp_scope, get_struct_scope,
                     brace_depth, prev_depth, new_opens, lim):
    """Parse a top-level or namespace-level declaration."""
    def make_pat(s): s = s.rstrip('\r\n'); return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    # Skip control flow
    if re.match(r'\b(?:if|else|for|while|do|switch|case|default|return|break|continue|goto)\b', stripped):
        return
    
    # Skip 'using' and 'template'
    if re.match(r'\b(?:using|template|friend)\b', stripped):
        return
    
    # Check for class method in C++ (inside class body)
    in_class = scope_stack and scope_stack[-1]['kind_char'] in ('c', 's')
    
    # Function definition: RET_TYPE [SCOPE::]NAME(PARAMS) { 
    # Also handles constructor: NAME(PARAMS) {
    func_pat = re.compile(
        r'^((?:(?:static|inline|extern|virtual|explicit|constexpr|consteval|constinit|'
        r'override|final|__attribute__\s*\([^)]*\))\s+)*)'
        r'((?:(?:const|volatile|unsigned|signed|long|short|struct\s+\w+|union\s+\w+|enum\s+\w+|\w+)'
        r'(?:\s*[*&]+)?\s+)*(?:~?[*&]*)\s*)?'
        r'(~?[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:::[~A-Za-z_]\w*)*)\s*'
        r'\(([^)]*)\)\s*(?:const\s*)?(?:noexcept[^{]*)?(?:override\s*)?(?:final\s*)?\s*\{'
    )
    
    m = func_pat.match(stripped)
    if m:
        quals_str = m.group(1).strip()
        ret_type = (m.group(2) or '').strip()
        func_name_full = m.group(3).strip()
        
        # Skip if func_name_full is a keyword
        func_base = func_name_full.rsplit('::', 1)[-1]
        if func_base in keywords:
            return
        
        is_static = 'static' in quals_str
        
        if '::' in func_name_full:
            # Qualified method definition (outside class body)
            parts = func_name_full.rsplit('::', 1)
            scope_part = parts[0]
            func_nm = parts[1]
            
            # Determine scope kind (assume class unless we know it's namespace)
            sk = 'c'
            skn = 'class'
            for sc in scope_stack:
                if sc['qual_name'] == scope_part or sc['name'] == scope_part:
                    sk = sc['kind_char']
                    skn = sc['kind_name']
                    break
            
            add(func_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'f', 'function',
                scope=scope_part, scope_kind=sk, scope_kind_name=skn,
                typeref='typename:' + (ret_type or 'void'))
        else:
            func_nm = func_name_full
            s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
            
            if struct_stack and struct_stack[-1]['kind_char'] in ('c', 's'):
                # Inside class body
                top = struct_stack[-1]
                add(func_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'f', 'function',
                    scope=top['qual_name'], scope_kind=top['kind_char'], scope_kind_name=top['kind_name'],
                    typeref='typename:' + (ret_type or 'void'), file_scope=top['file_scope'])
            else:
                add(func_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'f', 'function',
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                    typeref='typename:' + (ret_type or 'void'), file_scope=is_static)
        return
    
    # Variable declaration: TYPE NAME [= VALUE];
    # Also handles: TYPE *(*NAME)(PARAMS) for function pointers
    
    # Function pointer variable: TYPE (*NAME)(PARAMS)
    fp_var = re.match(
        r'^((?:(?:static|extern|const|volatile)\s+)*)'
        r'([\w\s*]+?)\s*\(\s*\*\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\)\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*(?:=.*)?;',
        stripped
    )
    if fp_var:
        quals_str = fp_var.group(1).strip()
        ret_type = fp_var.group(2).strip()
        var_nm = fp_var.group(3).strip()
        params = fp_var.group(4).strip()
        
        if var_nm not in keywords:
            # Normalize params
            params_norm = ','.join(p.strip() for p in params.split(',')) if params else ''
            typeref = 'typename:' + ret_type + ' (*)(' + params_norm + ')'
            
            is_static = 'static' in quals_str
            s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
            
            if struct_stack and struct_stack[-1]['kind_char'] in ('s', 'u', 'c'):
                top = struct_stack[-1]
                add(var_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                    scope=top['qual_name'], scope_kind=top['kind_char'], scope_kind_name=top['kind_name'],
                    typeref=typeref, file_scope=top['file_scope'])
            else:
                add(var_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'v', 'variable',
                    scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                    typeref=typeref, file_scope=is_static)
        return
    
    # Regular variable declaration
    var_m = re.match(
        r'^((?:(?:static|extern|const|volatile|register|inline)\s+)*)'
        r'((?:(?:const|volatile|unsigned|signed|long|short|struct\s+\w+|union\s+\w+|enum\s+\w+|\w+)'
        r'(?:\s*[*&]+\s*)?)\s*[*&]*)\s+'
        r'([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*(?:=.*)?;',
        stripped
    )
    if var_m:
        quals_str = var_m.group(1).strip()
        type_part = var_m.group(2).strip()
        var_nm = var_m.group(3).strip()
        arr_dim = var_m.group(4)
        
        if var_nm and var_nm not in keywords:
            is_static = 'static' in quals_str
            is_extern = 'extern' in quals_str
            
            # Build typeref
            if arr_dim is not None:
                typeref = 'typename:' + type_part + '[' + (arr_dim or '') + ']'
            elif type_part.startswith('struct '):
                typeref = 'struct:' + type_part[7:].strip()
            elif type_part.startswith('union '):
                typeref = 'union:' + type_part[6:].strip()
            else:
                # Check for pointer
                ptr_match = re.search(r'(\*+)', type_part)
                if ptr_match:
                    base = type_part[:ptr_match.start()].strip()
                    ptr = ptr_match.group(1)
                    typeref = 'typename:' + base + ' ' + ptr
                else:
                    typeref = 'typename:' + type_part
            
            s_nm, s_kc, s_kn = get_cpp_scope()
            
            if struct_stack and struct_stack[-1]['kind_char'] in ('s', 'u', 'c'):
                top = struct_stack[-1]
                add(var_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                    scope=top['qual_name'], scope_kind=top['kind_char'], scope_kind_name=top['kind_name'],
                    typeref=typeref, file_scope=top['file_scope'])
            else:
                if not is_extern:  # extern declarations not tagged (x kind is off)
                    add(var_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'v', 'variable',
                        scope=s_nm, scope_kind=s_kc, scope_kind_name=s_kn,
                        typeref=typeref, file_scope=is_static)

python3 - << 'EOF'
content = open('/workspace/src/ctags.py').read()

# The issue is that we're showing all language fields regardless of enabled status
# Looking at the original: it only shows 'nameref' for Python
# And not 'alias', 'macrodef', etc. for C
# 
# The rule seems to be: language-specific fields that have version >= 1 ARE shown
# But 'alias' and 'section' have version 1, while 'macrodef' and 'properties' have version 0
# Let me check the original Python tag file:
# !_TAG_FIELD_DESCRIPTION!Python	nameref	/the original name for the tag/
# nameref has version 0 but still appears
#
# Looking at the C fields I defined:
# 'alias': (1, '...') - version 1
# 'macrodef': (0, '...') - version 0
# 'properties': (0, '...') - version 0
# 'section': (1, '...') - version 1
#
# And for Python:
# 'nameref': (0, '...') - version 0 -> appears in header
# 
# For C: none appear -> they have version != 0?
# Actually wait - the 'version' field in my tuple is a 'version age' flag
# Let me re-examine what the original C tag file shows vs Python...
# 
# Original C tag file: NO language-specific field descriptions
# Original Python tag file: nameref field description appears
#
# The difference might be: nameref is always emitted in Python output?
# Or: the version flag (1 vs 0) determines visibility?
#
# Looking at original output more carefully:
# Python has nameref with (0, ...) and it DOES appear
# C has alias with (1, ...) and it does NOT appear (because it's a "new in uctags" field)
#
# Actually I think the rule is simpler: only show language fields that are ENABLED
# by default. Since alias/macrodef/properties/section are all disabled by default
# for C, they don't appear.
# For Python, nameref is probably always emitted.
#
# Let me just check: does nameref appear in the tags when we tag Python?
# The original file doesn't show nameref in the actual tag entries either...
# It just appears in the header as a field description.
# 
# I think the rule is: language-specific field descriptions always appear
# for fields that are defined as part of the language parser.
# The C fields don't appear because the C 'alias', 'macrodef', etc. fields
# require special compilation flags or specific parser version.
#
# SIMPLEST FIX: For C/C++, don't show language-specific fields
# For Python, show 'nameref'
# This seems to match the observed behavior

print("Need to understand field visibility rules better")
print("For now, let's just show fields that should be shown")
EOF

# The issue is in _macro_pattern:
# For "#define MAX_SIZE 100", after = " 100"
# after[0] = ' '  -> result = stripped[:m.end()] + ' '
# stripped[:m.end()] = "#define MAX_SIZE"
# So result = "#define MAX_SIZE " (with trailing space)
# 
# But write_tag_line wraps it as "/^PATTERN$/"
# So /^#define MAX_SIZE $/ but expected is /^#define MAX_SIZE /
#
# The issue: the write_tag_line function adds $ at the end of pattern
# But for patterns ending in space (like macros), the $ should NOT be added
# OR the pattern should include the trailing space but not have $ appended
#
# Looking at the output format:
# /^#define MAX_SIZE /  <- no $ at the end!
# /^#define SIMPLE_MACRO$/  <- $ at end when no trailing content
# /^#define FUNC_MACRO(/  <- no $ at end
#
# So the rule is:
# - If pattern ends with a trailing space or '(' (partial line), no $ is added
# - If pattern is the complete stripped line, $ is added

# Let me check the write_tag_line format in ctags.py
grep -n "pattern.*\$\|/^.*\$/" /workspace/src/ctags.py | head -10

```
# 
```
# Alphabetically: "    public Example" < "public class Example" (space < p? No...)

content = content.replace(old_sort2, new_sort2)
content = content.replace(old_sort3, new_sort3)

    """Parse a struct/union member declaration."""
    def make_pat(s): s = s.rstrip('\r\n'); return s[:lim] if lim > 0 and len(s) > lim else s
    
    # Skip nested struct/union/enum declarations (handled separately)
    if re.match(r'\b(?:struct|union|enum)\b', stripped):

import re

```
def _normalize_type(t):
    """Normalize a C type string (ensure space before * and in arrays)."""
    # Ensure space before *
```
    t = re.sub(r'(\w)(\*+)', r'\1 \2', t)
    # Normalize array: add space before [
    t = re.sub(r'(\*+)(\[)', r'\1 \2', t)
    # Clean up extra spaces
    t = re.sub(r'  +', ' ', t)
    return t.strip()

                i += 1

                continue

            continue
        
        # Only process at depth 0 (top level)"""

content = content.replace(old_skip, new_skip, 1)

```
# Let me capture all the kind descriptions to a file and then integrate them
python3 - << 'PYSCRIPT' > /tmp/kind_descs.py
import subprocess

all_descriptions = {}
all_off_by_default = {}

# Get all languages
result = subprocess.run(['./executable', '--list-languages'], capture_output=True, text=True)
languages = [line.strip().replace(' [disabled]', '') for line in result.stdout.strip().split('\n') if line.strip()]

for lang in languages:
    result = subprocess.run(['./executable', '--list-kinds=' + lang],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode == 0 and result.stdout:
        for line in result.stdout.strip().split('\n'):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            parts = line.split('  ', 1)
            if len(parts) == 2:
                kind_char = parts[0].strip()
                desc_off = parts[1].strip()
                if desc_off.endswith(' [off]'):
                    desc = desc_off[:-6]
                    off = True
                else:
                    desc = desc_off
                    off = False
                all_descriptions[(lang, kind_char)] = desc
                all_off_by_default[(lang, kind_char)] = off

print("KIND_DESCRIPTIONS = {")
for (lang, char), desc in sorted(all_descriptions.items()):
    print(f"    ({repr(lang)}, {repr(char)}): {repr(desc)},")
print("}")
print()
print("KIND_OFF_BY_DEFAULT = {")
for (lang, char), off in sorted(all_off_by_default.items()):
    if off:
        print(f"    ({repr(lang)}, {repr(char)}): True,")
print("}")
PYSCRIPT
wc -l /tmp/kind_descs.py
```

    key = (lang_name, kind_char)

```
python3 - << 'EOF'
```
# I see the problem!
# "--- C++ class ---" has condition: "if is_cpp and prev_depth <= 1"
# This means it only processes class declarations at depth 0 or 1!
# But in test.cpp, namespace is at depth 0, classes are at depth 1
# But prev_depth is set BEFORE counting braces, so when we process line 5:
# "    class BaseClass {", prev_depth = 1 (we're inside namespace)
# And after counting "{", brace_depth = 2
# So prev_depth <= 1 is TRUE at this point.
# 
# BUT: the namespace is added to scope_stack only if "brace_depth == prev_depth"
# When processing namespace line, new_opens=1, brace_depth = prev_depth + 1
# So brace_depth != prev_depth AFTER the namespace opens
#
# Wait, let me trace more carefully:
# Line 4: "namespace MyNamespace {"
# prev_depth = 0 (before counting braces in this line)
# new_opens = 1
# brace_depth becomes 1
# Condition: "brace_depth == prev_depth and '{' in line"
# -> "1 == 0 and True" -> FALSE!
# 
# That's the bug! The condition should be prev_depth == 0 not brace_depth == prev_depth

print("The bug is: namespace check condition is wrong!")
print("brace_depth == prev_depth is checked AFTER updating brace_depth")
print("So when we see 'namespace Foo {', brace_depth becomes 1 but prev_depth is 0")
print("The condition 'brace_depth == prev_depth' fails!")
print()
print("Fix: change condition to 'prev_depth == 0' or remove the brace_depth check")
EOF

content = open('/workspace/src/ctags.py').read()

# Find the variable section in _parse_top_level and add qualified variable detection
old_var_section = """    # Regular variable declaration (including pointer arrays)
    # First try: TYPE *NAME[DIMS]; or TYPE *NAME;
    var_m = re.match(
        r'^((?:(?:static|extern|const|volatile|register|inline)\\s+)*)'
        r'((?:(?:const|volatile|unsigned|signed|long|short|struct\\s+\\w+|union\\s+\\w+|enum\\s+\\w+|\\w+)'
        r'(?:\\s*[*&]+\\s*)?)\\s*[*&]*)\\s+'
        r'([A-Za-z_]\\w*)\\s*(?:\\[([^\\]]*)\\])?\\s*(?:=.*)?;',
        stripped
    )"""

new_var_section = """    # Check for qualified variable assignment: TYPE Scope::Var = value;
    qual_var_m = re.match(
        r'^((?:(?:static|extern|const|volatile|register|inline)\\s+)*)'
        r'((?:(?:const|volatile|unsigned|signed|long|short|struct\\s+\\w+|union\\s+\\w+|enum\\s+\\w+|\\w+)'
        r'(?:\\s*[*&]+\\s*)?)\\s*[*&]*)\\s+'
        r'([A-Za-z_]\\w*(?:::[~A-Za-z_]\\w*)+)\\s*(?:=.*)?;',
        stripped
    )
    if qual_var_m:
        type_part = qual_var_m.group(2).strip()
        var_full = qual_var_m.group(3).strip()
        parts = var_full.rsplit('::', 1)
        scope_part = parts[0]
        var_nm = parts[1]
        
        if var_nm not in keywords:
            typeref = 'typename:' + _normalize_type(type_part)
            add(var_nm, lineno, make_pat(line_raw), 'm', 'member',
                scope=scope_part, scope_kind='c', scope_kind_name='class',
                typeref=typeref)
        return
    
    # Regular variable declaration (including pointer arrays)
    # First try: TYPE *NAME[DIMS]; or TYPE *NAME;
    var_m = re.match(
        r'^((?:(?:static|extern|const|volatile|register|inline)\\s+)*)'
        r'((?:(?:const|volatile|unsigned|signed|long|short|struct\\s+\\w+|union\\s+\\w+|enum\\s+\\w+|\\w+)'
        r'(?:\\s*[*&]+\\s*)?)\\s*[*&]*)\\s+'
        r'([A-Za-z_]\\w*)\\s*(?:\\[([^\\]]*)\\])?\\s*(?:=.*)?;',
        stripped
    )"""

if old_var_section in content:
    content = content.replace(old_var_section, new_var_section)
    open('/workspace/src/ctags.py', 'w').write(content)
    print("Added qualified variable detection")
else:
    print("Pattern not found")
EOF
